Without it the draft is a flattering 'ambitious, shrewd' type that sits on top of the corpus's ambitious plus guarded, and its shadows (minds reputation, hides the soft side) weigh less than Gryffindor's 'act first and think later'. (31 words; 'dark sense of humor' and 'appearance' give way.)

The Hat's line must first be recorded in source_text from a fetchable page (the writer could not: Fandom 402, Wikiquote lacks the song); Wikipedia's 'Hogwarts' article, already a recorded source, may carry it. I quote it from memory and could not fetch either.

sets.name: VALS
sets.review: Agree on grain and shape: primary motivation, the person's outlook, then how one buys, 29 to 32 words, one 'This means being/living/leading'; the buying clause is on all eight and does tell thinker from believer and achiever from striver. Disagree that resources read off all three pairs: thinker 'comfortable' / believer 'of modest means' yes, innovator 'ample means' above and survivor 'fewest means' below yes, but achiever carries no 'successful' and maker no means marker at all, so the achiever/striver pair reads off striver alone and the experiencer/maker pair off 'spending freely' alone; the edits add both. Provenance: with SBI unreachable, four drafts carry SBI phrases that are not in their recorded passages (achiever 'to peers', innovator 'cultivated', thinker 'order, knowledge', striver 'copy what the better-off own', the last not flagged in notes). As far as I know they are accurate to SBI's segment pages, so the risk is provenance, not accuracy; the edits strip to the record, and the alternative is to seed as drafted and confirm at the SBI recheck the writer asks for (regeneration after an edit costs cents). Maker's 'suspicious of new ideas and large institutions': not now, same reason; at the recheck, where it would sharpen the experiencer/maker contrast (a 30-word version is in maker's issues). Strength: flattering by design for the high-resource four, as the source; all milder than the corpus's plain traits except experiencer, agreed.

sets.name: love languages
sets.review: Agree: one grain and shape ('feeling loved through X: what delights, what wounds'), 30 to 32 words, all for the receiver, each told from the others by channel and wound (insult; distraction and postponed dates; forgotten birthday or hasty gift; laziness and broken commitments; neglect). Two notes. The writer renders Chapman's 'can' flat in three members ('can leave you shattered' as 'shatters', 'can be especially hurtful' as 'are', 'can be unforgivable' as 'is'); I read it as the inside-voice equivalent of a modal that in this copy means 'does, for this person', uniform across the set and a notch above the letter of the hedge rule: a judgment call for Roger, not an edit. Physical touch is the one passage that describes the person's own behaviour ('very touchy') and the draft drops it; an optional restoration is given. Receiving gifts drops 'the absence of everyday gestures' (a second wound), tolerable at 32. Nearest-existing lines are right: nothing in the corpus is about the channel through which affection is received.

sets.name: VARK
sets.review: Agree: one grain (the channel, then Fleming's own list of materials), 30 to 32 words, neutral throughout, weaker than any plain corpus trait as a learning-preference instrument should be; visual's 'rather than' is justified by the polysemy of 'visual' and names no sibling. Two flags outside the drafts. (1) The label 'auditory (VARK)': Fleming's pole is 'Aural' (the A of VARK), and naming rule 1 says to use the standard's own pole names, so by the rule the label is 'aural (VARK)'; the writer kept the queue's word as instructed; Roger's call. (2) kinesthetic (VARK) beside the corpus's experiential ('drawing from practical examples, real-world case studies, concrete scenarios ... rather than relying solely on abstract theory'): the two share examples, case studies and practice over theory; experiential is how one argues, kinesthetic how one learns, and in a text persona both will show as reaching for cases. The writer's line lists experiential but contrasts only hands_on and concrete (and the corpus's hands_on is about staying in delegated work, not handiwork), so nearest_existing_ok is false for kinesthetic: say experiential is the near-duplicate and record it in source per rule 5.

sets.name: blood type
sets.review: Agree: virtues, then 'but also' and the faults, 23 to 29 words after the edits, all 'This means being', the folk balance mirrored and B's fault list the longest as Wikipedia's note on the minority types warrants; AB is defined relationally with A's and B's own adjectives and names neither; the deliberate drop of A's 'creativity' (Voyapon) to keep creative for B is a departure from the record that I endorse for legibility of the set. A set, not an axis structure; nothing to read off. Strength: B and O at source (hedges kept as 'at times', 'sometimes'); A and AB a notch off (A's 'sensitivity' narrowed to 'sensitive to others'; AB's 'very' and 'strongly' dropped), fixed by the edits. Wikipedia is thin (one clause per type), so the portraits rest mostly on a travel magazine; Roger should know that this set's source of record is weaker than the others'.

sets.name: Hogwarts houses
sets.review: Agree on grain and shape: virtue list, two or three behaviours from the official 'type of person' list, the shadow where the source gives one, 31 to 32 words; all four flattering by design and markedly more so than the corpus's plain traits, mirrored as the rule requires; Hufflepuff rightly has no shadow. On the flag: yes, sharpen Slytherin toward the books. The packet names the Sorting Hat's descriptions first for this system, the Hat's 'use any means to achieve their ends' is the canonical popular portrait and the most LLM-legible line about the house, and without it the draft is a flattering type near ambitious plus guarded whose shadows weigh less than Gryffindor's; wording (31 words) is in slytherin's issues, and the line must first be recorded in source_text from a fetchable page. Ravenclaw's 'quite eccentric' loses its softener (edit given). Gryffindor and Hufflepuff are faithful and complete.

summary: 25 drafts, all in form (23 to 32 words, every one opening 'This means', no system or author named, US spelling): 14 ok, 11 edit, nine of them one-word or one-phrase fixes (dropped intensifiers in blood types A and AB and in Ravenclaw; 'local' in believer; 'of modest means' and 'only' in maker; 'successful' in achiever; an optional 'very touchy' in physical touch). The two that matter: Slytherin should be sharpened toward the books with the Sorting Hat's 'use any means to achieve their ends' (31-word wording given; the line must first be recorded from a fetchable page), and the VALS set carries four SBI phrases not in its recorded passages (achiever, innovator, thinker, striver; accurate to SBI as far as I know, so provenance, not accuracy): the edits strip to the record, or seed as drafted and confirm at the SBI recheck. Maker's 'suspicious of new ideas and large institutions': not now, at the recheck; maker also lacks the low-resource marker the set_review promises. Sets: agree with the writer on all five sets' grain and shape; disagree only that VALS's resources read off all three pairs (not achiever/striver or experiencer/maker as drafted); the love languages render Chapman's 'can' flat throughout, a notch above the letter, uniform, Roger's call. Outside the drafts: 'auditory (VARK)' should be 'aural (VARK)' by naming rule 1 (Fleming's own pole name), and kinesthetic (VARK) is a near-duplicate of the corpus's experiential, which source should say.
